description: Empirical conversion model: base alkali conversion x FFA penalty (np.interp vs feedstock FFA%) x reaction-temperature multiplier (peak 60 C). Per-feedstock oil content gives biodiesel mass per tonne feed. Numbers reused from EC149 F1b.
source: Freedman et al. (1984); Meher et al. (2006); Rashid et al. (2008) — reused from EC149 F1b

base_conversion.note: Max alkali conversion at design conditions (low FFA)

ffa_penalty_curve.comment: Conversion multiplier vs feedstock FFA (%). Base-catalysed yield drops ~2% per %FFA above 1% (Rashid 2008). Clamped to 1.0 at low FFA.

feedstock_table.comment: Oil content (mass frac of feed) and FFA% per feedstock, reused verbatim from EC149 F1b.

temperature_curve.comment: Conversion multiplier vs reaction temperature (degC), peak at 60 C.
